items.note: DWP.5 'ι-real systems' and 'twist reductions used when weights are real'. Used in Outline D: ℱ₀ is a direct factor of the ι-real ℱ₀ ⊕ ℱ₀^∨ when of weight 0.

items.name: Setting of (1.3): X₀ normal geometrically connected of finite type over F_q
items.statement: The conventions (0.7) are in force. X₀ is a normal geometrically connected scheme of finite type over F_q and x̄ a geometric point of X₀.
items.note: Setting only.

items.name: Image of π₁(X, x̄) in W(X₀, x̄)^ab is (finite prime-to-p) × (pro-p)
items.statement: Théorème (1.3.1). The image of the geometric fundamental group π₁(X, x̄) in the quotient of W(X₀, x̄) by the closure of its derived group is the product of a finite group of order prime to p by a pro-p-group.
items.note: Proved here only for X a curve (the only case needed for the main results); the general case is treated in (1.11.4). No atlas stage plans it (searched 'abelian', '1.3.1' in DWP/LPV/FA). Its curve proof consumes FA.4 class field theory and finiteness of Pic⁰ (next items).

items.name: Class field theory: W(X₀, x̄)^ab ≅ (∏_{v∉S} r_v^*)\k_A^*/k^* (curve case)
items.statement: Let X̄₀ be the smooth projective completion of the curve X₀, S = X̄₀ − X₀, k the function field of X₀, k_v its completion at a place v (identified with a closed point v ∈ |X̄₀|), r_v [the ring of integers; printed 'the group of units'] of k_v and k_A^* the idèle group of k. Class field theory identifies W(X₀, x̄)^{ab} with the idèle class group (∏_{v∉S} r_v^*)\k_A^*/k^*, the projective limit of the divisor class groups C_m = {divisors on X₀}/{those of the form (φ) with φ ≡ 1 (m)} for m a larger and larger 'modulus' concentrated on S. The image of the geometric fundamental group is obtained by replacing k_A^* by the subgroup k_A^1 of idèles of norm 1, i.e. the C_m by the subgroups C_m^0 of classes of divisors of degree 0.
items.note: Recalled input. FA.4: 'construct the global reciprocity map from ideles, show principal ideles act trivially, and identify every finite abelian quotient by its norm subgroup ... Relate the degree map to the Galois group of constants and establish ray class fields with conductor data.' FA.2: 'Export the compact degree-zero idele class group'.

items.name: Curve case of (1.3.1): the kernel is a quotient of ∏_{v∈S} r_v^*
items.statement: The kernel of (∏_{v∉S} r_v^*)\k_A^1/k^* → (∏_v r_v^*)\k_A^1/k^* is a quotient of ∏_{v∈S} r_v^*, hence is the product of a pro-p-group and a finite group; the image ∏_v r_v^*\k_A^1/k^* is the group of classes of divisors of degree 0 for linear equivalence.
items.note: Elementary idelic computation (units of a local field of characteristic p = finite prime-to-p group × pro-p principal units). Not in the library; FA.2 'Export the compact degree-zero idele class group separately' provides the objects but no phrase states this.

items.name: Recalled (Weil, BNT IV Th. 7): the group of degree-0 divisor classes of a function field over F_q is finite
items.statement: The group of classes of divisors of degree 0, for linear equivalence, is finite (Weil, BNT IV, Th. 7). (The Picard variety Pic⁰ is of finite type, and this group is the group of F_q-rational points of Pic⁰ [of X̄₀].)
items.note: Tau Ceti: TauCeti.Divisor.finite_ker_degreeClass (TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/RiemannRoch/ClassNumber.lean:143), 'The degree-zero divisor class group Cl⁰(F) of an algebraic function field with a finite constant field is finite (Stichtenoth, Proposition 5.1.3)'. The parenthetical Picard-variety interpretation is not in the library (FA.1 plans 'finiteness of Pic^0(F_q)').

items.name: Convention from (1.3.2) on: 'faisceaux' are Weil sheaves; Q̄_ℓ-sheaves are 'faisceaux étales'
items.statement: (1.3.2) In the rest of the article, 'sheaves' (faisceaux) means Weil sheaves (1.1.10). Constructible Q̄_ℓ-sheaves are called étale sheaves. This convention will sometimes lead to applying to Q_ℓ-sheaves results proved for Q̄_ℓ-sheaves; the justification is always immediate.
items.note: DWP.5 'distinguish Weil descent from continuous Galois descent'.

items.name: Rank-one Weil sheaves ↔ characters χ: W(X₀, x̄) → Q̄_ℓ^*; the sheaf ℒ₀(χ)
items.statement: (1.3.3) Let ℱ₀ be a sheaf of rank 1 on X₀. The group W(X₀, x̄) acts on ℱ_x̄ by homotheties, via a character χ: W(X₀, x̄) → Q̄_ℓ^*. Conversely, for every such character χ, the equivalence (1.1.12) provides a sheaf ℒ₀(χ) with a trivialisation ℒ(χ)_x̄ ∼ Q̄_ℓ. The character χ factors through the largest abelian quotient of W(X₀, x̄).
items.note: DWP.5 (rank-one Weil sheaves; 'distinguish Weil descent from continuous Galois descent'). No explicit phrase for characters.

items.name: Proposition (1.3.4)(i): rank-one lisse sheaves have finite geometric monodromy; χ = c^{deg} · (finite order)
items.statement: Proposition (1.3.4). Let ℱ₀ be a lisse sheaf of rank 1 on X₀ and χ: W(X₀, x̄) → Q̄_ℓ^* the corresponding character. (i) The geometric monodromy group of ℱ₀ is finite. More precisely, the character χ is the product of a character w ↦ c^{deg(w)} by a character of finite order.
items.note: Proof (1.3.3): by (1.3.1) the image χ(π₁(X, x̄)) is (finite)×(pro-p) and a compact subgroup of E^* (E finite over Q_ℓ), hence (finite)×(pro-ℓ), hence finite as p ≠ ℓ; so χⁿ is trivial on π₁(X, x̄), i.e. χⁿ = b^{deg}, and with cⁿ = b, χ = c^{deg}·ε, ε of order n. No stage phrase plans it; DWP.5's scope ('Weil II §§1.2–1.11') covers it only as a source range.

items.name: Proposition (1.3.4)(ii): rank-one lisse sheaves are ι-pure of weight w_q(c)
items.statement: (1.3.4)(ii). ℱ₀ is punctually ι-pure, of weight the weight of c, rel. q. (Indeed |ιχ(F_y)| = |ιc|^{deg(y)} for y ∈ |X₀|.)
items.note: Consequence of (i) and (1.1.13). Not planned by a stage phrase (see (i)). Used throughout §1.3 and in (1.3.9).

items.name: Variant (after N. Katz): (1.3.4) in general from the curve case
items.statement: Variante. If X₀ is a curve the proof of (1.3.1) is complete, independent of (1.11), whence (1.3.4). Katz's deduction of the general case: let E ⊂ Q̄_ℓ be as above and M the (finite) group of elements of finite order of E^*. For x and y in |X₀| one has χ(F_x)^{1/deg(x)} = χ(F_y)^{1/deg(y)} in E^* ⊗ Q (joining x and y by a curve, apply (1.3.4) for curves). Hence for every 0-cycle of degree 0 Σn(x)x, χ(∏F_x^{n(x)}) ∈ M. By Čebotarev's theorem these products of Frobenius are dense in the geometric π₁, so χ maps it into M: the restriction of χ to the geometric π₁ has finite order, and one concludes as before.
items.note: Inputs: existence of a curve through two closed points of a connected normal X₀ (not planned) and Čebotarev density for schemes of finite type over F_q (DWP.3 plans 'the function-field closed-point Chebotarev/density input in §6.13' for curves; FA.5 'Prove a function-field Chebotarev statement'; the higher-dimensional density used here is not planned).

items.name: Determinantal weights (rel. ι) of a lisse sheaf
items.statement: Definition (1.3.5). Let ℱ₀ be a lisse sheaf on X₀. The determinantal weights (rel. ι) of ℱ₀ are the numbers (1/d)(ι-weight of Λ^d 𝒢₀) for 𝒢₀ a constituent of ℱ₀ and d its rank. A lisse punctually ι-pure sheaf of weight β is clearly also purely of determinantal weight β.
items.note: Key new notion of §1.3; no atlas stage names determinantal weights (searched 'determinantal', 'determinant weight'). DWP.5's source range 'Weil II §§1.2–1.11' includes it, and its phrase 'irreducible constituents' is where it would live.

items.name: (1.3.6): twisting an irreducible lisse sheaf to determinantal weight 0 with finite-order determinant
items.statement: (1.3.6) If ℱ₀ is lisse, irreducible of rank n, and b ∈ Q̄_ℓ^* [printed Q_ℓ^*] is such that for some y ∈ |X₀| one has det(F_y) = b^{n deg(y)[F_q : F_p]}, then the sheaf ℱ₀^{(b⁻¹)} (1.2.7) is of determinantal weight 0 (rel. ι) for every ι: its maximal exterior power is defined by a character of finite order.
items.note: DWP.5: 'Prove the coefficient-embedding and twist reductions used when weights are real.' Uses (1.3.4)(i).

items.name: Algebraic monodromy groups G⁰ ⊂ G of a lisse sheaf (diagram (1.3.7.1))
items.statement: (1.3.7) (Dictionary inspired by Serre [11], II (1.3).) Let ℱ₀ be a lisse sheaf on X₀ and G⁰ the algebraic subgroup of GL(ℱ_x̄) which is the Zariski closure of the geometric monodromy group (1.1.15). By push-out from 0 → π₁(X, x̄) → W(X₀, x̄) → Z → 0 one defines an algebraic group (not of finite type) G, extension of Z by G⁰, with a map G → GL(ℱ_x̄) (diagram (1.3.7.1)). Exact definition: if w ∈ W(X₀, x̄) has degree 1, W(X₀, x̄) is the semidirect product of w^Z by π₁(X, x̄); the image w̄ of w in GL(ℱ_x̄) normalises the geometric monodromy group, hence its Zariski closure G⁰, and G is the semidirect product of Z by G⁰ relative to the action int(w̄) of Z on G⁰. G is characterised up to unique isomorphism by fitting in a diagram (1.3.7.1).
items.note: No stage plans algebraic monodromy groups of lisse sheaves over finite fields (searched 'Zariski closure', 'monodromy group', 'algebraic monodromy'; only MordellLawrenceVenkatesh for a different setting).

items.name: Representations of G give Weil sheaves; sums of sheaves and products of GL's
items.statement: Each linear representation of the algebraic group G defines an ℓ-adic representation of W(X₀, x̄), hence a Weil sheaf on X₀; the original sheaf ℱ₀ corresponds to the tautological representation (1.3.7.1) of G in GL(ℱ_x̄). If ℱ₀^{(i)} is a finite family of lisse sheaves and the construction is applied to the sum ℱ₀ of the ℱ₀^{(i)}, one can replace GL(ℱ_x̄) in (1.3.7.1) by the subgroup ∏GL(ℱ_x̄^{(i)}); each ℱ₀^{(i)} is determined by the representation of G in the corresponding factor GL(ℱ_x̄^{(i)}).

items.name: Théorème (1.3.8) (Grothendieck): the radical of G⁰⁰ is unipotent
items.statement: Théorème (1.3.8) (Grothendieck). Let ℱ₀ be a lisse sheaf on X₀, G and G⁰ as above and G⁰⁰ the identity component of G⁰. Then the radical of the algebraic group G⁰⁰ is unipotent.
items.note: Proof on p. 160: with a Jordan–Hölder series of ℱ₀, P its stabiliser in GL(ℱ_x̄), N the unipotent radical acting trivially on graded pieces, L = P/N: G⁰ ⊂ P, the analogue G⁰₁ for Gr(ℱ₀) is the image of G⁰ in L, and G⁰ is an extension of G⁰₁ by a (unipotent) subgroup of N; so reduce to Gr(ℱ₀), justiciable of (1.3.9). No atlas stage plans it.

items.name: Corollaire (1.3.9): for ℱ₀ semisimple, G⁰ is an extension of a finite group by a semisimple group
items.statement: Corollaire (1.3.9). If ℱ₀ is semisimple, the Zariski closure G⁰ of the geometric monodromy group of ℱ₀ is an extension of a finite group by a semisimple group.
items.note: Proved (before (1.3.8)) assuming only that the representation of π₁(X, x̄) is semisimple (which follows: the sum of simple π₁-submodules is W-stable, so has a complement). Then G⁰⁰ is reductive and one shows its largest central torus T₁, isogenous to the largest torus quotient T of G⁰⁰, is trivial: if G⁰ = G⁰⁰ and G ≃ G⁰⁰×Z, the maps W(X₀, x̄) → T have Zariski-dense image of π₁(X, x̄), finite by (1.3.4), so T = {1}; the general case reduces to this by a finite cover of X₀ and a finite extension of F_q (W acts on T₁ through a finite quotient since it preserves the finite set of characters of T₁ on ℱ₀x̄, which generates X(T₁); outer automorphisms of G⁰⁰ trivial on T₁ form a finite group). No atlas stage plans it.

items.name: Semisimple W-representations restrict to semisimple π₁-representations
items.statement: If the representation of W(X₀, x̄) on ℱ₀x̄ is semisimple, so is its restriction to the normal subgroup π₁(X, x̄): the sum of the simple π₁(X, x̄)-submodules is W-stable, hence has a complement, and so on.
items.note: Clifford-type argument; not in Mathlib in this form and not planned by a stage phrase.

items.name: Lemme (1.3.10): four equivalent conditions for an extension G of Z by G⁰ with G⁰⁰ reductive
items.statement: Lemme (1.3.10). Let G be a group scheme which is an extension of Z by an algebraic group G⁰ whose identity component G⁰⁰ is reductive. The following conditions are equivalent: (i) G admits a linear representation whose restriction to G⁰ is faithful; (ii) G admits a linear representation whose restriction to G⁰ has finite kernel; (iii) let Z⁰⁰ be the identity component of the centre of G⁰⁰; the restriction to Z⁰⁰ of every inner automorphism of G has finite order; (iv) the centre of G maps onto a subgroup of finite index of Z (printed 'sur un sous-groupe fini de Z', see PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E10).
items.note: Proof: (i)⇒(ii) trivial; (ii)⇒(iii): the weights of Z⁰⁰ in the representation form a finite G-stable set generating X(Z⁰⁰)⊗Q; (iii)⇒(iv): via Aut(reductive) = (pinning-preserving) ⋉ (adjoint) and finite order detected on the connected centre, modify g of degree 1 so Int(g)|G⁰ has finite order n, then gⁿ is central; (iv)⇒(i): a central Z generated by g of degree n ≠ 0 gives an algebraic G/Z whose faithful representations work. No atlas stage plans it.

items.name: Recalled: Aut of a reductive group = pinning-preserving automorphisms ⋉ inner; finite order detected on connected centre
items.statement: The group of automorphisms of a reductive group is the semidirect product of the group of automorphisms respecting a pinning (épinglage) by the adjoint group (inner automorphisms) (SGA 3 XXIV (1.3)); and an automorphism respecting a pinning has finite order if and only if its restriction to the connected centre does.
items.note: Recalled from SGA 3 (printed 'XXXIV'; (PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E9, PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E10)). Tau Ceti's ReductiveGroups roadmap layer 9 constructs pinnings ('This is what makes "the" graph automorphism well defined'), and RG2.5 an action on a pinning, but no stage phrase states the Aut(G) = Aut(G, pinning) ⋉ G^ad decomposition.

items.name: Corollaire (1.3.11): kernel and cokernel of deg: Z → Z are finite for ℱ₀ semisimple
items.statement: Corollaire (1.3.11). Suppose ℱ₀ semisimple and let Z be the centre of G. Then the kernel and cokernel of deg: Z → Z are finite.
items.note: Proof: the kernel Z∩G⁰ is contained in the centre of G⁰, finite by (1.3.9); by (1.3.9) again Z⁰⁰ = {e}, so (1.3.10)(iii) holds and the cokernel is finite by (1.3.10)(iv). Not planned.

items.name: Corollaire (1.3.12): determinantal ι-weight via eigenvalues of a central element of degree m
items.statement: Corollaire (1.3.12). Suppose ℱ₀ semisimple and let g be a central element of G of degree m ≠ 0. For the sheaf defined by a representation V of G to be purely of determinantal ι-weight β, it is necessary and sufficient that the eigenvalues α of g acting on V all satisfy |ια| = q^{mβ/2}.
items.note: Proof: reduce to V simple, where g is scalar; replace V by its maximal exterior power to reduce to rank 1, left to the reader (cf. (1.3.4)). Not planned by a stage phrase.

items.name: Proposition (1.3.13)(i): determinantal weight is detected after dominant pullback
items.statement: Proposition (1.3.13)(i). Let f: X'₀ → X₀ be a dominant morphism of normal connected schemes of finite type over F_q. For a lisse sheaf on X₀ to be purely of determinantal ι-weight β, it is necessary and sufficient that its inverse image on X'₀ be so.
items.note: Main result of §1.3 (per p. 161); plays the role of symplectic invariant theory of (I.3.2) in the generalisation (1.5.1). DWP.5: 'Construct Weil II's generalization of the fundamental estimate for ι-real systems, irreducible constituents and compatible pairings'; no phrase names determinantal weights.

items.name: Proposition (1.3.13)(ii): determinantal weights add under tensor product
items.statement: (1.3.13)(ii). If lisse sheaves ℱ₀ and 𝒢₀ on X₀ are purely of determinantal ι-weight β and γ, then ℱ₀ ⊗ 𝒢₀ is purely of determinantal ι-weight β+γ. (For (ii), take G defined by ℱ₀ and 𝒢₀ ((1.3.7), last paragraph).)

items.name: Proposition (1.3.13)(iii): determinantal weights of Λ^a ℱ₀
items.statement: (1.3.13)(iii). Let ℱ₀ be a lisse sheaf on X₀ and n(β) the sum of the ranks of the constituents of ℱ₀ of determinantal ι-weight β. Then the determinantal weights of Λ^a ℱ₀ are the Σ a(β)β with Σ a(β) = a and a(β) ≤ n(β) [a(β) ≥ 0 integers].

items.name: Proposition (1.3.14): an irreducible lisse Weil sheaf is étale iff its determinant is; every irreducible lisse sheaf is a twist of an étale one
items.statement: Proposition (1.3.14) (see (1.3.2)). For an irreducible lisse sheaf ℱ₀ of rank r on X₀ to be an étale sheaf, it is necessary and sufficient that Λ^r ℱ₀ be one. Every irreducible lisse sheaf is therefore obtained by torsion (1.2.7) from an étale sheaf.
items.note: Proof: g central as in (1.3.12) acts on ℱ₀x̄ by a scalar u; Λ^r ℱ₀ is étale iff u is an ℓ-adic unit; then with W(X₀,x) acting through GL(r,E) one shows the image is bounded (W₁ = inverse image of G⁰⁰×g^Z, ρ: W₁ → G⁰⁰; ρ(W₁) normalises the compact Zariski-dense ρ(W₁⁰)) by Lemma (1.3.15), so the representation extends to the completion π₁(X₀, x). Used in (1.1.11) to extend Grothendieck's results to Weil sheaves. DWP.5: 'distinguish Weil descent from continuous Galois descent' and 'twist reductions'.

items.name: Lemme (1.3.15): normaliser of a compact Zariski-dense subgroup of a semisimple group over a local field is compact
items.statement: Lemme (1.3.15). In a semisimple group H over a local field E, the normaliser of a compact Zariski-dense subgroup K ⊂ H(E) is compact.
items.note: Proved only for E of characteristic 0 (enough here, E finite over Q_ℓ): the logarithm, defined near e, extends to the union of compact subgroups by log(x) = (1/n) log(xⁿ); density of K and semisimplicity of H imply log(K) spans Lie H over E; the 𝒪_E-module L⁰ generated by the compact log K ⊂ Lie H is stable under the normaliser of K; ad: H(E) → GL(Lie H) has finite kernel and is proper, so the normaliser is compact. LPV.5 'Build the necessary ℓ-adic analytic matrix-group/closed-subgroup and exponential-logarithm lemmas if unavailable' is related but does not plan this lemma.

items.name: H⁰ and H⁰_c of a sheaf on a curve
items.statement: Let X be a curve over an algebraically closed field k and 𝓕 a sheaf on X. H⁰(X,𝓕) is the group of global sections and H⁰_c(X,𝓕) the subgroup of those with compact support (finite support if X has no complete irreducible component). If X is connected with base point x and 𝓕 is lisse, defined by a representation V of π₁(X,x), then (1.4.1.1) H⁰(X,𝓕) = V^{π₁(X,x)}; (1.4.1.2) H⁰_c(X,𝓕) = V^{π₁(X,x)} if X is complete, 0 otherwise.
items.note: Planned under the atlas convention (as in the accepted Weil I extraction PAPER-DELIGNE-74) for the upstream CohomologicalPointCounting (PR196) suppliers, which have no atlas stage of their own: SF.2 'Integrate CohomologicalPointCounting suppliers ... construct sheaf cohomology, localization, proper/smooth base change and compact support'. Weil I analogue PAPER-DELIGNE-74 (2.9.1)/(2.10)(i). Recalled 'well-known' fact; used via (1.4.2) for the poles of L-functions in (1.4.3) and throughout §1.5, §1.8.

items.name: H²_c of a curve via an open and coinvariants
items.statement: If U is the complement of a finite subset of X, H²_c(U,𝓕) ⥲ H²_c(X,𝓕). Taking U small enough that U_red is smooth and 𝓕 lisse on U, this allows computing H²_c by Poincaré duality from a): if U_red is smooth connected with base point x and on U 𝓕 is defined by a representation V of π₁(U,x), then (1.4.1.3) H²_c(X,𝓕) = V_{π₁(U,x)}(−1) (coinvariants, Tate-twisted by −1).
items.note: DWP.2: 'Use Poincaré duality to calculate H²_c of these tensor powers' (Weil I 2.10(ii) planned there, PAPER-DELIGNE-74); excision for H_c from Planned under the atlas convention (as in the accepted Weil I extraction PAPER-DELIGNE-74) for the upstream CohomologicalPointCounting (PR196) suppliers, which have no atlas stage of their own: SF.2 'Integrate CohomologicalPointCounting suppliers ... construct sheaf cohomology, localization, proper/smooth base change and compact support'.

items.name: H⁰, H⁰_c, H²_c of a lisse sheaf on a curve over F_q via its largest geometrically constant sub/quotient
items.statement: With conventions (0.7), let X₀ be a smooth absolutely irreducible curve over F_q and 𝓕₀ a lisse sheaf on X₀. Let 𝓕₀′ (resp. 𝓕₀″) be the largest subsheaf (resp. quotient sheaf) of 𝓕₀ that becomes constant on X; it is the inverse image of a sheaf F₀′ (resp. F₀″) on Spec(F_q), and (1.4.1) gives (1.4.2.1) H⁰(X,𝓕) = F′; (1.4.2.2) H⁰_c(X,𝓕) = F′ or 0 according as X is or is not complete; (1.4.2.3) H²_c(X,𝓕) = F″(−1). The sheaves 𝓕₀′ and F₀′ (resp. 𝓕₀″ and F₀″) have the same determinantal weights, and these are among the determinantal weights of 𝓕₀.
items.note: Frobenius-equivariant form of (1.4.1); the determinantal-weight claim uses (1.3.5) (determinantal weights, other section) and that 𝓕₀′ is a subobject/𝓕₀″ a quotient. DWP.5: 'Construct Weil II's generalization of the fundamental estimate for ι-real systems, irreducible constituents and compatible pairings, then the Hadamard–de la Vallée-Poussin positivity argument ... Prove convergence, poles, multiplicities, tensor-power compatibility and the weight-integrality detection step' (Sources: 'Weil II §§1.2–1.11'). Printed 'D'après (1.4.2)' at the foot of p. 162 introducing Cor. (1.4.3).

items.name: Weights of Frobenius on H⁰, H⁰_c, H²_c are determinantal weights
items.statement: If α is an eigenvalue of F* on H⁰(X,𝓕) or H⁰_c(X,𝓕) (resp. H²_c(X,𝓕)), there exists a determinantal weight β of 𝓕₀ with w_q(α) = β (resp. w_q(α) = β+2).
items.note: Immediate from (1.4.2). Controls the poles of the right side of (1.4.7.2), used in (1.5.2) b) and (1.8.1) b). DWP.5: 'Construct Weil II's generalization of the fundamental estimate for ι-real systems, irreducible constituents and compatible pairings, then the Hadamard–de la Vallée-Poussin positivity argument ... Prove convergence, poles, multiplicities, tensor-power compatibility and the weight-integrality detection step' (Sources: 'Weil II §§1.2–1.11').

items.name: Eigenvalues on H⁰, H²_c are local Frobenius eigenvalues
items.statement: If α is an eigenvalue of F* on H⁰(X,𝓕) or H⁰_c(X,𝓕) (resp. H²_c(X,𝓕)), then for every x ∈ |X₀|, α^{deg(x)} (resp. (q⁻¹α)^{deg(x)}) is an eigenvalue of F_x on 𝓕₀.
items.note: 'More trivially' from (1.4.2): F′ (resp. F″) is a subquotient of each stalk. DWP.5: 'Construct Weil II's generalization of the fundamental estimate for ι-real systems, irreducible constituents and compatible pairings, then the Hadamard–de la Vallée-Poussin positivity argument ... Prove convergence, poles, multiplicities, tensor-power compatibility and the weight-integrality detection step' (Sources: 'Weil II §§1.2–1.11').

items.name: Grothendieck's cohomological formula for the L-function
items.statement: If X₀ is a scheme of finite type over F_q and 𝓕₀ a sheaf on X₀, one has (Grothendieck) the equality of ℓ-adic formal series (1.4.5.1) ∏_{x∈|X₀|} det(1 − F_x t^{deg x}, 𝓕)⁻¹ = ∏_i det(1 − F t, H^i_c(X,𝓕))^{(−1)^{i+1}}. Applying ι gives an equality of complex formal series expressing that the left side is the Taylor expansion of the rational function on the right; if the left product converges for |t| < R, one obtains an equality of analytic functions in that disc.
items.note: Planned under the atlas convention (as in the accepted Weil I extraction PAPER-DELIGNE-74) for the upstream CohomologicalPointCounting (PR196) suppliers, which have no atlas stage of their own: SF.2 'Integrate CohomologicalPointCounting suppliers ... construct sheaf cohomology, localization, proper/smooth base change and compact support' and WC.1 'Consume the coefficientwise Euler product and determinant formula'. Same as Weil I (1.14.3) in PAPER-DELIGNE-74 (planned WC.1, SF.2).

items.name: Convergence criterion for the Euler product
items.statement: If for x ∈ |X₀| the eigenvalues α of F_x on 𝓕 satisfy w_{N(x)}(α) ≤ β, the product ∏ ι det(1 − F_x t^{deg x}, 𝓕)⁻¹ converges for |t| < q^{−β/2 − dim X₀}, hence has neither zero nor pole in that disc.
items.note: Proof: put d = dim X₀; cutting X₀ into pieces quasi-finite over A^d₀ gives (number of x ∈ |X₀| of degree n) ≤ C^{te}·q^{dn}, reducing to the geometric series Σ_n q^{nd}·q^{nβ/2}·|t|^n. Generalises Weil I (3.8) (PAPER-DELIGNE-74, planned DWP.2). DWP.5: 'Construct Weil II's generalization of the fundamental estimate for ι-real systems, irreducible constituents and compatible pairings, then the Hadamard–de la Vallée-Poussin positivity argument ... Prove convergence, poles, multiplicities, tensor-power compatibility and the weight-integrality detection step' (Sources: 'Weil II §§1.2–1.11').

items.name: Crude bound on the number of closed points of given degree
items.statement: For X₀ of finite type over F_q with d = dim X₀: (number of points x ∈ |X₀| of degree n) ≤ C^{te}·q^{dn}, obtained by cutting X₀ into pieces each quasi-finite over an affine space A^d₀.
items.note: Key unnumbered fact in the proof of (1.4.6). DWP.5 'Prove convergence'; WC.1 exposes point-count arithmetic ('N_r=∑_{m|r} m a_m'). No library statement.

items.name: L-function formula on a curve
items.statement: If dim X₀ ≤ 1, H^i_c = 0 for i ≠ 0,1,2, and (1.4.5.1) after ι becomes (1.4.7.1) ∏_{x∈|X₀|} ι det(1 − F_x t^{deg x}, 𝓕)⁻¹ = ι det(1 − Ft, H¹_c(X,𝓕)) / (ι det(1 − Ft, H⁰_c(X,𝓕)) · ι det(1 − Ft, H²_c(X,𝓕))). If X₀ is a smooth affine curve and 𝓕₀ is lisse, H⁰_c = 0 and the formula simplifies to (1.4.7.2) ∏_{x∈|X₀|} ι det(1 − F_x t^{deg x}, 𝓕)⁻¹ = ι det(1 − Ft, H¹_c(X,𝓕)) / ι det(1 − Ft, H²_c(X,𝓕)). In use, the left side is controlled by (1.4.6) and the poles on the right by (1.4.3).
items.note: Cohomological-dimension vanishing and H⁰_c = 0 from Planned under the atlas convention (as in the accepted Weil I extraction PAPER-DELIGNE-74) for the upstream CohomologicalPointCounting (PR196) suppliers, which have no atlas stage of their own: SF.2 'Integrate CohomologicalPointCounting suppliers ... construct sheaf cohomology, localization, proper/smooth base change and compact support'; formula from WC.1 (trace formula). Used in (1.5.2.1) and (1.8.1.1).

items.name: Constituents of an ι-real lisse sheaf are ι-pure
items.statement: (Conventions (0.7).) Let X₀ be a smooth absolutely irreducible curve over F_q. The constituents of every ι-real lisse sheaf on X₀ are ι-pure.
items.note: Generalises Weil I Theorem (3.2) with a parallel proof. Proof in (1.5.3) from (1.5.2) applied to exterior powers and the identity (1.5.3.1). DWP.5: 'Construct Weil II's generalization of the fundamental estimate for ι-real systems, irreducible constituents and compatible pairings, then the Hadamard–de la Vallée-Poussin positivity argument ... Prove convergence, poles, multiplicities, tensor-power compatibility and the weight-integrality detection step' (Sources: 'Weil II §§1.2–1.11').

items.name: Local weights bounded by the largest determinantal weight
items.statement: Let 𝓕₀ be an ι-real lisse sheaf on X₀ and r the largest of its determinantal weights (rel. ι) (1.3.5). Then for every x ∈ |X₀| and every eigenvalue α of F_x on 𝓕, W_{N(x)}(α) ≤ r.
items.note: Proof: remove a point to make X₀ affine; for each k>0 use (1.5.2.1) = (1.4.7.2) for ⊗^{2k}𝓕. a) the local factors ι det(1 − F_x t^{deg x}, ⊗^{2k}𝓕₀)⁻¹ are formal series with constant term 1 and real coefficients ≥ 0 (as in Weil I (3.3),(3.4) with 'rational' replaced by 'real'); b) by (1.3.13)(ii) the determinantal weights of the constituents of ⊗^{2k}𝓕₀ are ≤ 2kr, so by (1.4.3) the right side has no pole for |t| < q^{−(2kr+2)/2}. By Weil I (3.5),(3.6) the local factors then have no pole there, giving |ια|^{2k/deg x} ≤ q^{(2kr+2)/2}, i.e. w_{N(x)}(α) ≤ r + 1/k; let k → ∞. DWP.5: 'Construct Weil II's generalization of the fundamental estimate for ι-real systems, irreducible constituents and compatible pairings, then the Hadamard–de la Vallée-Poussin positivity argument ... Prove convergence, poles, multiplicities, tensor-power compatibility and the weight-integrality detection step' (Sources: 'Weil II §§1.2–1.11').

items.name: Nonnegativity of local factors for even tensor powers of an ι-real sheaf
items.statement: For 𝓕₀ ι-real lisse and k ≥ 1, the factors ι det(1 − F_x t^{deg x}, ⊗^{2k}𝓕₀)⁻¹ are formal series with constant term 1 and real coefficients ≥ 0.
items.note: Proved as in Weil I (3.3), (3.4) with 'rational' replaced by 'real' (planned for Weil I at DWP.2: 'local trace powers are rational and nonnegative ... nonnegative local Euler-factor coefficients'). DWP.5 plans the ι-real version: 'Weil II's generalization of the fundamental estimate for ι-real systems'.

items.name: Proof of (1.5.1): eigenvalue weights on the β-part equal β
items.statement: Let 𝓕₀ be ι-real lisse on X₀. For β ∈ ℝ let 𝓕₀(β) be the sum of the constituents of 𝓕₀ of determinantal weight β (rel. ι) and n(β) its rank; for x ∈ |X₀| let α_i^β (1 ≤ i ≤ n(β)) be the eigenvalues of F_x on 𝓕(β) with multiplicity. By definition of determinantal weight, (1.5.3.1) Σ_i w_{N(x)}(α_i^γ) = n(γ)·γ for every γ. With N = Σ_{γ>β} n(γ) and (1.3.13)(iii), the determinantal weights of Λ^{N+1}𝓕₀ are ≤ β + Σ_{γ>β} n(γ)·γ; since each α_i^β·∏_{γ>β}∏_i α_i^γ is an eigenvalue of F_x on Λ^{N+1}𝓕₀, (1.5.2) gives (1.5.3.2) w_{N(x)}(α_i^β) ≤ β, and summing over i against (1.5.3.1) (or passing to the dual) gives w_{N(x)}(α_i^β) = β.
items.note: Uses exterior powers (1.3.13)(iii) from §1.3 (other section). DWP.5: 'Construct Weil II's generalization of the fundamental estimate for ι-real systems, irreducible constituents and compatible pairings, then the Hadamard–de la Vallée-Poussin positivity argument ... Prove convergence, poles, multiplicities, tensor-power compatibility and the weight-integrality detection step' (Sources: 'Weil II §§1.2–1.11').

items.name: Monodromy filtration of a nilpotent endomorphism (existence and uniqueness)
items.statement: Let N be a nilpotent endomorphism of an object V of an abelian category. There exists one and only one finite increasing filtration (0.10) M of V such that N M_i ⊂ M_{i−2} and N^k induces an isomorphism Gr^M_k V ⥲ Gr^M_{−k} V (k ≥ 0).
items.note: Existence by induction on d with N^{d+1} = 0 (uniqueness 'proved likewise'); see the construction item. LPV.1: 'Construct the uniquely characterized monodromy filtration centered at a specified integer: N lowers the filtration by two and N^r identifies opposite graded pieces with the appropriate twist. Prove this linear algebra and its functorial properties' (sources: 'the linear-algebra conventions in Deligne II §§1.6–1.7'). Library audit: 'Neither library has this linear algebra; the only weight filtrations in Tau Ceti belong to mixed Hodge structures and are not built from a nilpotent operator.' LPV.1 is phrased for the ℓ-adic vector-space setting; the paper's statement is for any abelian category (used in (1.6.13) and with Weil sheaves).

items.name: Inductive construction of the monodromy filtration
items.statement: Induction on d with N^{d+1} = 0. For d = 0 (N = 0), M is trivial (Gr^M_i V = 0 for i ≠ 0). Otherwise put M_d = V, M_{d−1} = Ker N^d, M_{−d} = Im N^d and M_{−d−1} = 0, so Gr^M_d V and Gr^M_{−d} V are the coimage and image of N^d. On Ker N^d / Im N^d the d-th power of N induces 0; this defines M on Ker N^d / Im N^d by induction, and M_i on V (d−1 ≥ i ≥ −d) is defined as the inverse image in Ker N^d of the subobject M_i of Ker N^d / Im N^d.
items.note: LPV.1: 'Construct the uniquely characterized monodromy filtration centered at a specified integer: N lowers the filtration by two and N^r identifies opposite graded pieces with the appropriate twist. Prove this linear algebra and its functorial properties' (sources: 'the linear-algebra conventions in Deligne II §§1.6–1.7'). Library audit: 'Neither library has this linear algebra; the only weight filtrations in Tau Ceti belong to mixed Hodge structures and are not built from a nilpotent operator.'

items.name: Monodromy filtration is compatible with passing to the dual category
items.statement: The characterisation (1.6.1) of M shows its compatibility with passage to the dual (opposite) category.
items.note: Used for (1.6.9)(ii). LPV.1: 'Construct the uniquely characterized monodromy filtration centered at a specified integer: N lowers the filtration by two and N^r identifies opposite graded pieces with the appropriate twist. Prove this linear algebra and its functorial properties' (sources: 'the linear-algebra conventions in Deligne II §§1.6–1.7'). Library audit: 'Neither library has this linear algebra; the only weight filtrations in Tau Ceti belong to mixed Hodge structures and are not built from a nilpotent operator.'

items.name: Primitive part P_i(V)
items.statement: The primitive part P_i(V) (or simply P_i) of Gr^M_i V is the kernel of the morphism induced by N from Gr^M_i V to Gr^M_{i−2} V.
items.note: Not named in LPV.1's plan (which covers the filtration and graded isomorphisms only). Convention: primitive parts live in non-positive degrees (P_i = 0 for i > 0), opposite to the usual 'ker N^{i+1} on Gr_i, i ≥ 0' convention. Used in (1.8.4).

items.name: Primitive (Lefschetz) decomposition of Gr^M
items.statement: If i > 0, N : Gr^M_i V → Gr^M_{i−2} V is injective (since N^{i−1}∘N is an isomorphism), so P_i = 0. If i ≥ 0, since N∘N^{i+1} : Gr^M_{i+2}V → Gr^M_{−i}V → Gr^M_{−i−2}V is an isomorphism, Gr^M_{−i}V is the direct sum of P_{−i} and of the image of Gr^M_{i+2} under N^{i+1}, and N maps this image isomorphically onto Gr^M_{−i−2}V. By decreasing induction on i ≥ 0 one gets an isomorphism of Gr^M_{−i}V with the sum of the P_{−j} for j ≥ i, j ≡ i mod 2; using further N^i : Gr^M_i V ⥲ Gr^M_{−i} V one obtains isomorphisms (1.6.4.1) Gr^M_i V ≃ ⊕_{j≥|i|, j≡i(2)} P_{−j}. Via these, N : Gr^M_i V → Gr^M_{i−2} V is the evident inclusion for i ≥ 1 (i−2 ≥ −1) and the evident projection for i−2 ≤ −1.
items.note: Not planned explicitly (LPV.1 plans the filtration and 'functorial properties', DWP.0 cites Weil II §1.6 as a source but plans only eigenvalue-weight linear algebra). The diagram on p. 166 labels the summand P_{−j} by 'P_j'. Twisted canonical form (1.6.14.3) is used in (1.8.4).

items.name: N is strictly compatible with the monodromy filtration
items.statement: The morphism N : (V, M) → (V, M shifted by 2) is strictly compatible with the filtrations, i.e. N M_{i+2} ⊃ Im(N) ∩ M_i.
items.note: Proof: if i < 0, N : M_{i+2} → M_i has surjective graded, hence is surjective; if i+2 > 0, N : V/M_{i+2} → V/M_i has injective graded, hence is injective, so N⁻¹M_i ⊂ M_{i+2}. Not named by LPV.1.

items.name: Gr^M of Ker N is the primitive part
items.statement: The inclusion of Ker N in V induces isomorphisms Gr^M_i(Ker N) ⥲ P_i (M induced on Ker N).
items.note: From strictness (1.6.5). Twisted form (1.6.14.2) is used in (1.8.4) to compare invariants (fibre of j_*) with primitive parts. Not named by LPV.1.

items.name: Monodromy filtration of a single Jordan block and in general
items.statement: Let V be finite-dimensional over a field k, and suppose that in a basis e the matrix of N is the lower-shift matrix (1.6.7.1) (ones just below the diagonal). Put dim V = d+1 and index the basis vectors by the integers from d to −d in steps of 2, so that N e_i = e_{i−2} for i ≠ −d and N e_{−d} = 0. Then M_i is spanned by the e_j for j ≤ i. In general V is a sum of N-stable subspaces V_α with N of type (1.6.7.1) on V_α, and the filtration M of V is the sum of the above filtrations of the V_α.
items.note: Mathlib has no Jordan normal form for nilpotent endomorphisms in this form; not in LPV.1's text. Printed 'dans une base e de N' and 'pour i ≠ d' (PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E12, PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E13).

items.name: Monodromy filtration via Jacobson–Morozov
items.statement: If k has characteristic 0, M can be interpreted via the Jacobson–Morozov theorem: if u : SL(2) → GL(V) satisfies du(0 0; 1 0) = N and V_j is the subspace of vectors v with u(diag(λ, λ⁻¹))(v) = λ^j v, then M_i is the sum of the V_j for j ≤ i. (Reduce to V an irreducible representation of SL(2), i.e. a symmetric power of the standard representation, which is the situation of (1.6.7).) This interpretation gives the behaviour of M under tensor product and duals (for which one may rather invoke (1.6.2)).
items.note: Existence of u (Jacobson–Morozov) is cited, not proved; no atlas stage plans Jacobson–Morozov (grep: the AdoIwasawa roadmap explicitly keeps it 'out of the dependency graph'). Mathlib has `IsSl2Triple` (Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/Sl2.lean:22) but no Jacobson–Morozov theorem.

items.name: Irreducible representations of SL(2) are the symmetric powers
items.statement: In characteristic 0, an irreducible finite-dimensional representation of SL(2) is a symmetric power of the evident (standard) representation; in a suitable basis N = du(0 0;1 0) has the form (1.6.7.1).
items.note: Recalled fact. Tau Ceti proves the Lie-algebra form (the one used, via du): TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Sl2/Classification.lean:216 `existsUnique_nonempty_lieModuleEquiv`: over a char-0 field, a finite-dimensional triangularizable irreducible sl(Fin 2) K-module is equivalent to the standard module V(n) (`Sl2Std K n`, dimension n+1) for exactly one n; complete reducibility TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Sl2/Decomposition.lean:68 `exists_isInternal_lieModuleEquiv` (K algebraically closed). The identification of V(n) with Sym^n of the standard representation and the group SL(2) version are not stated.

items.name: Tensor product and dual of nilpotent-endomorphism pairs
items.statement: The tensor product (V,N) of (V′,N′) and (V″,N″) is V = V′⊗V″, N = N′⊗1 + 1⊗N″; the dual of (V′,N′) is (V′*, −ᵗN′).
items.note: DWP.5 'tensor and dual compatibility'; LPV.1 'its functorial properties'.

items.name: Monodromy filtration of a tensor product
items.statement: If k has characteristic 0, the filtration M of a tensor product is the tensor product of the filtrations M of the factors: M_i(V′⊗V″) = Σ_{i′+i″=i} M_{i′}(V′)⊗M_{i″}(V″).
items.note: Via (1.6.8) (Jacobson–Morozov). DWP.5 'tensor and dual compatibility'; LPV.1 'functorial properties'. Used for 𝓕₀⊗𝓕₀ in (1.8.4).

items.name: Monodromy filtration of a dual
items.statement: The filtration M of a dual is the dual of the filtration M of the original space: M_i(V*) = M_{−i−1}(V)^⊥.
items.note: By (1.6.2) (no characteristic hypothesis needed). DWP.5 'tensor and dual compatibility'.

items.name: Gr^M commutes with tensor product and dual
items.statement: Under these hypotheses, the formation of Gr^M is compatible with tensor product and with passage to the dual.
items.note: DWP.5 'tensor and dual compatibility'.

items.name: Canonical SL(2)-representation on Gr^M V
items.statement: Assume V finite-dimensional over k of characteristic 0. On Gr^M(V) there is a unique representation v of SL(2) such that dv(0 0;1 0) is N : Gr^M_* V → Gr^M_{*−2} V and diag(λ, λ⁻¹) acts by multiplication by λ^j on Gr^M_j(V). Existence: choose u as in (1.6.8), identify Gr^M_j(V) with V via the splitting V_j of the filtration and transport u. Uniqueness: Bourbaki, Lie VIII, §11, no. 1, lemma 1. The formation of v is compatible with tensor product and dual taken as in (1.6.9).
items.note: Cited inputs: Jacobson–Morozov (existence) and Bourbaki Lie VIII §11 no.1 lemma 1 (uniqueness of the sl2-triple completing a given (h, e)). Mathlib/Tau Ceti have `IsSl2Triple` but not this uniqueness lemma in this form. Used to derive (1.6.12).

items.name: Chosen irreducibles S_d, lowest weight vectors, and index set P(d,d′)
items.statement: Choose once and for all, for each integer d ≥ 0, an irreducible representation S_d of SL(2) of dimension d+1 and a lowest-weight vector e_{−d} ∈ S_d, e_{−d} ≠ 0, which diag(λ, λ⁻¹) sends to λ^{−d}e_{−d}. Put (1.6.11.1) P(d,d′) = {j | |d−d′| ≤ j ≤ d+d′ and j ≡ d ± d′ (2)}.
items.note: Tau Ceti's standard module `Sl2Std K n` (TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Sl2/Standard.lean, basis `basis`, `finrank_eq` at :433: dimension n+1) is the Lie-algebra version of S_d; the lowest weight vector is its last basis vector (`lower_basis_last`, :514). P(d,d′) itself is just the index set in Clebsch–Gordan.

items.name: Clebsch–Gordan decomposition
items.statement: There are isomorphisms of representations (1.6.11.2) S_d ⊗ S_{d′} ⥲ ⊕_{j∈P(d,d′)} S_j (choices fixed).
items.note: TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Sl2/ClebschGordan.lean:297 `isInternal_cgSummand` (the summands cgSummand K m n k, k ≤ min m n, form an internal direct sum of V(m)⊗V(n)) with :253 `nonempty_lieModuleEquiv_cgSummand` (the k-th is ≅ V(m+n−2k)); over a char-0 field, sl(Fin 2) K-modules (Lie-algebra form, as used via dv).

items.name: Self-duality of S_d
items.statement: There are isomorphisms of representations (1.6.11.3) S_d* ⥲ S_d (choices fixed).
items.note: Not found in Tau Ceti's Sl2 files (no dual-module statement); follows from the classification plus weights.

items.name: Gr^M V ≅ ⊕ S_j ⊗ P_{−j} and P_{−j} = Hom_{SL(2)}(S_j, Gr^M V)
items.statement: For V, N, M and P as above, there is a unique isomorphism of SL(2)-representations (1.6.11.4) α : ⊕_j S_j ⊗ P_{−j} ⥲ Gr^M(V), where SL(2) acts trivially on P_j at the source and by (1.6.9) [i.e. (1.6.10)] at the target, such that the composite P_{−j} →(e_{−j}⊗) S_j⊗P_{−j} →α Gr^M(V) is the identity inclusion of P_{−j}. This gives isomorphisms (1.6.11.5) P_{−j} ≃ Hom_{SL(2)}(S_j, Gr^M(V)).
items.note: Isotypic decomposition with primitive (lowest-weight) multiplicity spaces; Tau Ceti has complete reducibility (Decomposition.lean:68) but not this canonical form. The printed reference '(1.6.9)' for the target action should be (1.6.10) (PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E17).

items.name: Primitive parts of a tensor product
items.statement: Let V′, V″ be as in (1.6.10), V = V′⊗V″, and write P_j, P′_j, P″_j for P_j(V), P_j(V′), P_j(V″). The tensor product of the isomorphisms (1.6.11.4) for V′ and V″, composed with (1.6.11.2), gives ⊕(S_j ⊗ ⊕_{j∈P(j′,j″)} P′_{−j′}⊗P″_{−j″}) ⥲ Gr^M(V), whence an isomorphism depending only on the choices (1.6.11.2): (1.6.12.1) P_{−j} ⥲ ⊕_{j∈P(j′,j″)} P′_{−j′} ⊗ P″_{−j″}.
items.note: DWP.5 'tensor and dual compatibility'. Twisted form (1.6.14.4) is the key input in (1.8.4) (applied to 𝓕₀⊗𝓕₀).

items.name: Primitive parts of a dual
items.statement: For the dual one likewise finds isomorphisms, depending only on the choices (1.6.11.3): (1.6.12.2) P_{−j}(V*) ⥲ P_{−j}(V)*.
items.note: DWP.5 'tensor and dual compatibility'. Twisted form (1.6.14.5) used in (1.8.4).

items.name: Uniqueness of the relative monodromy filtration
items.statement: Let V be an object of an abelian category with a finite increasing filtration W, and N a nilpotent endomorphism of V respecting W. There exists at most one finite increasing filtration M of V such that N M_i ⊂ M_{i−2} and N^k induces isomorphisms Gr^M_{i+k} Gr^W_i V ⥲ Gr^M_{i−k} Gr^W_i V.
items.note: Proof: induction on the length of W, normalised to W₀ = V; the induced filtration on W_{−1} is determined; the quotient filtration is (1.6.1) for Gr^W_0 V; with c such that Gr^M_i Gr^W_0 V ≠ 0 only for −c ≤ i ≤ c one checks for i ≥ 0: 1) for i > c, M_{−i} = M_{−i}(W_{−1}); 2) M_{−i} = M_{−i}(W_{−1}) + N^i(M_i); 3) M_i = Ker(N^{i+1} : V → V/M_{−i−2}); descending induction on |i| then determines M from its restriction to W_{−1} and N. Existence is not claimed in general (it is proved in the geometric situation in (1.8.5), and posed for Hodge theory in Problem (1.8.15)). LPV.1 plans only the absolute filtration; no stage names the relative one ('filtration de monodromie locale rel. W').

items.name: Choice-free version with a 1-dimensional nilpotent Lie algebra 𝔑 and twists Y(k)
items.statement: In applications the abelian category is vector spaces over k of characteristic 0 and one has a nilpotent action of a 1-dimensional Lie algebra 𝔑 rather than an endomorphism; the theory applies on choosing N ≠ 0 in 𝔑. In (1.6.13) the existence of M, and M itself, are independent of N. For any vector space Y write Y(k) = Y ⊗ 𝔑^{⊗k}; N^k becomes a canonical isomorphism (1.6.14.1) Gr^M_{i+k} Gr^W_i V(k) ⥲ Gr^M_{i−k} Gr^W_i V. In the situation (1.6.1)–(1.6.12), M and P_j do not depend on N, but (1.6.4.1), (1.6.12.1–2) do; replacing N by λN multiplies each component α : X → Y by a suitable power λ^{−k}, and α⊗N^{⊗k} : X → Y(k) is independent of N.
items.note: In (1.7.2) the twist (k) becomes a Tate twist and 𝔑 = ℚ_ℓ(1)-line. LPV.1: 'N^r identifies opposite graded pieces with the appropriate twist', 'independence under change of a tame generator after interpreting N:V→V(-1)'.

items.name: Gr^M_i(Ker N) ≃ P_i (choice-free)
items.note: Canonical version of (1.6.6); used in (1.8.4).

items.name: Canonical primitive decomposition with twists
items.statement: (1.6.14.3) Gr^M_i V ≃ ⊕_{j≥|i|, j≡i(2)} P_{−j}(−(i+j)/2) (for (1.6.4.1)); the print has the twist (i+j)/2, see PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E15.
items.note: Mnemonic (p. 170): regarding Gr_i and P_i as of weight i and 𝔑 as of weight −2, both sides are isobaric of the same weight. With Y(k) = Y⊗𝔑^{⊗k} of weight (weight Y) − 2k, P_{−j}((i+j)/2) has weight −i−2j ≠ i; the correct twist is −(i+j)/2 (PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E15). Used to conclude (1.8.4).

items.name: Canonical primitive parts of a tensor product with twists
items.note: Canonical (Tate-twisted) form of (1.6.12.1); used in (1.8.4) with j = 0, j′ = j″: P_{−j}⊗P_{−j}(−j) is a direct factor of P₀ of the tensor square. DWP.5 'tensor and dual compatibility'.

items.name: Canonical primitive parts of a dual with twist
items.note: Used in (1.8.4) for the lower bound. DWP.5 'tensor and dual compatibility'.

items.name: Inertia group (local monodromy group) of a henselian DVR
items.statement: Let R be a henselian discrete valuation ring, K its fraction field, k = R/𝔪 its residue field, K̄ an algebraic closure of K and k̄ the residue field of the normalisation of R in K̄ (an algebraic closure of k); it is often convenient to choose k̄ first, then K̄ as an algebraic closure of the fraction field of the strict henselisation of R rel. k̄ (cf. (0.6)). The inertia group I is defined by the exact sequence (1.7.1.1) 0 → I → Gal(K̄/K) → Gal(k̄/k) → 0. It, or its image in a representation, is also called the local monodromy group.
items.note: LPV.1: 'Construct tame/wild inertia and the tame character t_ℓ:I→Z_ℓ(1) using the existing ramification and roots-of-unity APIs.' R01.2 plans the local-field version.

items.name: Wild inertia and the tame character t_ℓ
items.statement: If k has characteristic exponent p, there is an exact sequence ([10], [5] §2) 0 → P → I →(t) Ẑ_{(p′)}(1) → 0 with P a pro-p-group; the quotient Ẑ_{(p′)}(1) = ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ(1) is the tame inertia group. Taking the ℓ-component of t gives t_ℓ : I → Z_ℓ(1), whose kernel is a profinite group of order prime to ℓ.
items.note: Cited ([10] Serre, Corps locaux; [5]). LPV.1 as quoted.

items.name: Logarithm of the unipotent part of local monodromy
items.statement: Let ρ : I → GL(V) be an ℓ-adic representation of I. Hypothesis (*): the restriction of ρ to a subgroup I₁ of finite index of I is unipotent (Grothendieck showed it often holds in practice, SGA 7 I). If so, there is a unique nilpotent representation ρ̄ of ℚ_ℓ(1), viewed as a 1-dimensional Lie algebra, in V such that (1.7.2.1) ρ(σ) = exp(ρ̄ t_ℓ(σ)) for σ ∈ I₁ ⊂ I. ρ̄ is called the logarithm of the unipotent part of the local monodromy; it may be identified with a nilpotent morphism N : V(1) → V, and the definition reads (1.7.2.2) ρ(σ) = exp(N·t_ℓ(σ)) for σ ∈ I₁ ⊂ I.
items.note: LPV.1: 'For a proved unipotent action, define N through the finite logarithm and prove nilpotence, independence under change of a tame generator after interpreting N:V→V(-1), and exp(t_ℓ(σ)N)=ρ(σ).' Mathlib has the nilpotent exponential (`IsNilpotent.exp`, Mathlib/RingTheory/Nilpotent/Exp.lean:55) but no unipotent logarithm (library audit).

items.name: Local monodromy filtration (and relative to W)
items.statement: The theory (1.6.14) applies with the twist (k) a Tate twist. The filtrations (1.6.1) and (1.6.13) of V (defined by N) are called respectively the local monodromy filtration of V and the local monodromy filtration of V rel. W.
items.note: Absolute case: LPV.1 'Construct the uniquely characterized monodromy filtration'; DWP.5 'Import LPV's inertia, nilpotent logarithm and monodromy-filtration carriers'. The relative version rel. W is not named in any stage. Printed reference '(1.6.14), (1.6.15)': there is no (1.6.15) (PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E18).

items.name: Weil group W(K̄/K) of a henselian DVR with finite residue field
items.statement: Suppose the residue field finite with q elements. The Weil group W(K̄/K) is the subgroup of Gal(K̄/K) which is the inverse image of W(k̄/k).
items.note: Class field theory roadmap Layer 9 'the local Weil group' builds it for local fields (from 'the exact sequence 1 → I_K → G_K → Ẑ → 1'); here R need only be henselian with finite residue field.

items.name: Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem for the Weil group
items.statement: Let V be an ℓ-adic representation of W(K̄/K) (finite residue field). By Grothendieck (SGA 7 I), condition (*) of (1.7.2) is automatically satisfied. The logarithm N : V(1) → V of the unipotent part of the monodromy is therefore defined, and it commutes with the action of W(K̄/K).
items.note: Cited from SGA 7 I. R01.2: 'For ℓ different from the residue characteristic, prove quasi-unipotence and construct the monodromy operator and Weil–Deligne representation, including independence of the tame character.' 'Commutes' means N is W-equivariant as a map V(1) → V.

items.name: Eigenvalues of two Frobenius lifts agree up to roots of unity
items.statement: If F′ and F″ are two lifts in W(K̄/K) of F ∈ W(k̄/k), the eigenvalues of F′ and F″ (on V) coincide up to multiplication by roots of unity.
items.note: Proof: replace V by its semisimplification, so the inertia action factors through a finite quotient; then F′^n and F″^n have the same image in GL(V) for some n > 0. Consequently the ι-weights (rel. q) of eigenvalues of F′ or F″ agree. DWP.5 'Frobenius–N relation' / 'weights of the monodromy graded pieces'.

items.name: Pure, mixed, ι-pure representations of W(K̄/K) and their weights
items.statement: Whatever ι, the ι-weights of the eigenvalues of F′ or F″ (rel. q) are the same. Imitating (1.2), one defines a pure, mixed, ι-pure representation (of W(K̄/K)) and the weights of a representation, using the eigenvalues of any Frobenius lift.
items.note: DWP.5 plans the sheaf-level 'punctually ι-pure/ι-mixed' notions and the local weight theorem; the local-representation notion is its local input.

items.name: Weight filtration of a representation of the local Weil group
items.statement: Suppose the ι-weights of V are integers. There exists one and only one finite increasing filtration M of V, stable under W(K̄/K), such that Gr^M_i(V) is ι-pure of weight i; it is called the weight filtration. One has N M_i(1) ⊂ M_{i−2}.
items.note: Proof: choose a Frobenius lift F′; let V′_i be the sum of generalised eigenspaces of F′ for eigenvalues α with w_q(α) = i, and M′_i = ∏_{j≤i} V′_j (printed j < i); N M′_i ⊂ M′_{i−2}. Independence of F′: for another lift F″ there is n > 0 with F′^n = F″^n mod I₁, so F″^n = exp(λN)F′^n for suitable λ ∈ ℚ_ℓ(−1), hence F″^n = exp(μN)F′^n exp(μN)⁻¹ with μ = λ/(1−q^n); exp(μN) carries M′ to M″ and N respects M′. DWP.5 'the Frobenius–N relation'.

items.name: ι-pure local representations have finite inertia image
items.statement: If V is ι-pure, the action of I factors through a finite quotient.
items.note: Proof: twist to integer weight; M has a single step, and N M_i ⊂ M_{i−2} forces N = 0. DWP.5 as quoted.

items.name: Decomposition of any local representation by eigenvalue classes
items.statement: The proof of (1.7.5) shows that any representation V admits a unique decomposition V = ΣV^α (α ∈ ℚ̄_ℓ*/(q^ℤ·roots of 1)) such that the eigenvalues of Frobenius lifts on V^α lie in α. Each V^α is obtained by twisting from a mixed representation.
items.note: Local analogue of the weight-class decomposition modulo ℤ (DWP.8 plans 3.4.1 for sheaves). DWP.5 as quoted.

items.name: Tame restriction functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕[E] along a normal crossings divisor
items.statement: Let D be a divisor with normal crossings of a regular scheme X, the transverse union of smooth divisors D_i (i ∈ I); localising, each D_i has a global equation t_i = 0; let E be the intersection of the D_i. For n invertible on X put X_n = X[t_i^{1/n}]_{i∈I} (the subscheme of affine space over X with coordinates T_i defined by T_i^n = t_i). π : X_n → X is étale over X − D and totally ramified over E; over E, π has the section t_i^{1/n} = 0, and restriction to E of a sheaf on X_n means inverse image by this section. (μ_n)^I acts on X_n by (r_i) acting on t_i^{1/n} by multiplication by r_i. Let 𝐋 be a set of primes invertible on X and 𝓕 a sheaf of sets on X − D, locally constant, tamely ramified along D and even 𝐋-ramified (for d the generic point of an irreducible component of D, X_(d) is a henselian trait; for η̄ a geometric generic point of it, inertia acts on 𝓕_η̄ through an 𝐋-group). Abhyankar's lemma gives n with all prime factors in 𝐋 such that the inverse image of 𝓕 on π⁻¹(X−D) ⊂ X_n is the restriction of a locally constant sheaf 𝓕̄ on X_n (the locally constant extension of 𝓕 to X_n). 𝓕[E] denotes the restriction of 𝓕̄ to E, with the action of μ_n^I induced from its action on X_n. With Z_𝐋(1) = ∏_{ℓ∈𝐋} Z_ℓ(1)_X (a pro-sheaf on E) this gives a functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕[E] from locally constant 𝐋-ramified sheaves of sets on X−D to locally constant sheaves of sets on E with an action of Z_𝐋(1)^I; it extends to constructible ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaves by passage to the limit (and to Weil sheaves).
items.note: Cited input: Abhyankar's lemma (AlgebraicCurves roadmap Layer 8 plans the field-theoretic form; LPV.5 uses 'the tame-cover specialization and Abhyankar-lemma argument' only for pencils). No atlas stage constructs this normal-crossings tame restriction functor. Used in (1.8.6)–(1.8.7) (|I| = 1) and §1.9.

items.name: Logarithms N_i of the unipotent part of the monodromy around D_i
items.statement: In many cases (see (1.7.12.1)), in particular if X is of finite type over ℤ, the action of Ẑ_𝐋(1)^I on 𝓕[E] is quasi-unipotent: there exist commuting nilpotent endomorphisms N_i in (End(𝓕[E]))(−1) such that σ in a suitable 'open' subsheaf nZ_𝐋(1)^I of Z_𝐋(1)^I acts by exp(ΣN_iσ_i). N_i is called the 'logarithm of the unipotent part of the monodromy around D_i'. For a smooth divisor (|I| = 1) this endomorphism defines, as before, the local monodromy filtration of 𝓕[D] (resp. rel. W).
items.note: Quasi-unipotence is asserted with a forward reference to (1.7.12.1); for X of finite type over ℤ it is Grothendieck's argument. LPV.1 plans N only on a henselian trait; no stage plans the normal-crossings sheaf version.

items.name: Iterated tame restrictions 𝓕[D*_J] and transitivity
items.statement: Near a p-fold intersection of the D_j, D is the union of p smooth divisors. For J ⊂ I, D_J is the intersection of the D_j (j ∈ J), X_J the complement of the union of the D_i (i ∉ J), D*_J = D_J ∩ X_J. (a) the D_i (i ∉ J) cut out on the regular scheme D_J a normal crossings divisor with complement D*_J; (b) the D_j (j ∈ J) cut out on X_J a normal crossings divisor with complement X − D, the intersection of whose traces is D*_J. For 𝓕 locally constant and 𝐋-ramified along D on X − D, (1.7.8) applied to (b) gives for each J a sheaf 𝓕[D*_J] on D*_J with an action of Z_𝐋^J(1); for suitable n it is the restriction to D*_J of the locally constant extension of 𝓕 to X_J[t_j^{1/n}] (j ∈ J). Choosing n so that 𝓕 has a locally constant extension to X_n = X[t_j^{1/n}(j∈J)][t_i^{1/n}(i∈I−J)] and restricting to the reduced inverse image D_J[t_i^{1/n}(i∈I−J)] shows 𝓕[D*_J] is 𝐋-ramified along the traces of the D_i (i ∉ J). This allows iterating: for K ⊂ I − J, 𝓕[D*_J][D*_{J∪K}] is a locally constant sheaf on D*_{J∪K} with actions of Z_𝐋^J(1) (by functoriality) and Z_𝐋^K(1). Transitivity of inverse images gives (1.7.9.1) 𝓕[D*_J][D*_{J∪K}] ≃ 𝓕[D*_{J∪K}], compatible with the actions of Z_𝐋(1)^{J∪K}; for J ⊂ K ⊂ L the square of these identifications (𝓕[D*_J][D*_K][D*_L] = 𝓕[D*_K][D*_L], 𝓕[D*_J][D*_L] = 𝓕[D*_L]) commutes. All this extends to constructible ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaves (and Weil sheaves) by passage to the limit.
items.note: Used only in §1.9 (not used later in the paper). No atlas stage.

items.name: Coordinate-free version via the normal bundle
items.statement: The constructions (1.7.8) depend on the choice of coordinates t_i. To canonify them, introduce the normal bundle T of E in X (a bundle of affine spaces over E) and the sub-bundles T_i tangent to the D_i, and replace 𝓕[E] by a sheaf 𝓕[E]′ on T − ∪T_i. A system of equations t_i defines a section of T − ∪T_i, and 𝓕[E] defined via the t_i is the inverse image of 𝓕[E]′ by this section. The construction is compatible with base change by a smooth morphism X₁ → X. The N_i and Z_𝐋(1)^I act on 𝓕[E]′, which plays the role of the restriction of 𝓕 to a tubular neighbourhood of E in X; it is an analogue of 'nilpotent orbits' in the theory of variations of Hodge structure.
items.note: Sketch only ('Indiquons brièvement'). No atlas stage.

items.name: Galois interpretation of the tame restriction over a henselian local base
items.statement: Suppose X henselian local, X = Spec(R), and 𝐋 the set of all primes invertible on X. Let k be the residue field of R, K its fraction field, R₁ a strict henselisation of R with residue field k₁ (a separable closure of k) and fraction field K₁, K̄ an algebraic closure of K₁ and K₂ ⊂ K̄ the extension of K₁ obtained by adjoining the n-th roots of the t_i for n invertible in R. A locally constant sheaf of sets on X − D is tamely ramified along D iff it becomes trivial on Spec(K₂); this identifies the tame fundamental group of X − D (base point Spec(K̄)) with Gal(K₂/K), an extension of Gal(K₁/K) = Gal(k₁/k) by Gal(K₂/K₁) = Ẑ_𝐋(1)^I: 0 → Z_𝐋(1)^I → π₁^mod(X−D, Spec(K̄)) → Gal(k₁/k) → 0. The choice of the t_i and t_i^{1/n} splits this extension (lift Gal(k₁/k) as the fixer of the t_i^{1/n}). A tamely ramified locally constant sheaf of sets 𝓕 on X − D, identified with a set F with π₁^mod-action, thus gives an action of Gal(k₁/k) on F and a Gal(k₁/k)-equivariant action of Ẑ_𝐋(1)^I, i.e. a sheaf on Spec(k) (or a locally constant sheaf on E) with an action of Z_𝐋(1)^I: this is 𝓕[E] of (1.7.8).
items.note: Tame fundamental group of the complement of a normal crossings divisor in a strictly local scheme (Abhyankar/SGA 1 XIII, cited implicitly). No atlas stage.

items.name: Tame Weil group W^mod(X−D, Spec K̄)
items.statement: If k is finite, W^mod(X−D, Spec(K̄)) is defined as the inverse image of W(k₁/k) in π₁^mod(X−D, Spec(K̄)).
items.note: Generalises (1.7.3). No atlas stage.

items.name: Quasi-unipotence of Z_𝐋(1)^I on W^mod-representations
items.statement: (Generalising (1.7.3)–(1.7.7), with the same proof.) The restriction to Z_𝐋(1)^I of an ℓ-adic representation V of W^mod(X−D, Spec(K̄)) is quasi-unipotent.
items.note: Grothendieck's argument (Frobenius conjugation raises tame inertia elements to the q-th power). R01.2/LPV.1 plan only the rank-one (trait) case.

items.name: Frobenius lifts in W^mod have the same eigenvalues up to roots of unity
items.statement: If F′ and F″ are two lifts in W^mod of F ∈ W(k₁/k), the eigenvalues of F′ and F″ coincide up to multiplication by roots of unity. This allows defining ι-weights etc. as in (1.7.4).
items.note: Analogue of (1.7.4); no stage plans the multi-divisor version.

items.name: Weight filtration for W^mod-representations
items.statement: If the ι-weights of V are integers, there is on V one and only one weight filtration M, as in (1.7.5). The analogues of (1.7.6) and (1.7.7) are true.
items.note: Analogue of (1.7.5)–(1.7.7). Used in §1.9 only.

items.name: Weights at the boundary of j_*𝓕₀ for a pure lisse sheaf on a curve
items.statement: (Conventions (0.7).) Let X₀ be a smooth absolutely irreducible curve over F_q (cf. (0.5)) and j : U₀ → X₀ an open subset, complement of the finite set of points S₀. If 𝓕₀ is a lisse sheaf on U₀, punctually ι-pure of weight β, then for every x ∈ |S₀| and every eigenvalue α of F_x on j_*𝓕₀, w_{N(x)}(α) ≤ β.
items.note: Proof: removing a point of U₀, assume X₀ affine; use (1.8.1.1) = (1.4.7.2) for j_*𝓕: ∏_{x∈|U₀|} ι det(1−F_x t^{deg x},𝓕₀)⁻¹ · ∏_{x∈|S₀|} ι det(1−F_x t^{deg x}, j_*𝓕₀)⁻¹ = ι det(1−Ft, H¹_c(X, j_*𝓕)) / ι det(1−Ft, H²_c(X, j_*𝓕)). a) by (1.4.6) the first factor converges and has no zero or pole for |t| < q^{−(β+2)/2}; b) by (1.4.3) the right side has no pole there; c) so the remaining local factors at S₀ have no pole there, giving |ια| ≤ N(x)^{(β+2)/2}, i.e. (1.8.1.2) w_{N(x)}(α) ≤ β+2. Apply to tensor powers: ⊗^k j_*𝓕₀ ⊂ j_*⊗^k𝓕₀, so w_{N(x)}(α^k) ≤ kβ+2, i.e. w_{N(x)}(α) ≤ β+2/k; let k → ∞. DWP.5: 'Import LPV's inertia, nilpotent logarithm and monodromy-filtration carriers. Prove the local weight theorem for a punctually pure lisse sheaf on an open curve, including the weights of the monodromy graded pieces and the weights of boundary invariants of j_*F. Include quasi-unipotent reduction, finite covers, tensor and dual compatibility and the Frobenius–N relation' (Sources: 'especially 1.8.4').

items.name: Weights of H¹_c(X, j_*𝓕) are ≤ β+2
items.statement: Comparing zeros of the two sides of (1.8.1.1): the left side has none for |t| < q^{−(β+2)/2} and the denominator on the right does not vanish there, so the numerator cannot vanish there; hence for every eigenvalue α of F on H¹_c(X, j_*𝓕), w_q(α) ≤ β+2.
items.note: Crude initial bound (the sharp bound β+1 is §3). DWP.5: 'the strict initial H¹ weight bound needed to start §3.2 ... The boundary estimates and strict bound are proved here'.

items.name: Local fibre at a boundary point and its local monodromy filtration
items.statement: Let s̄ ∈ S with image s in S₀, η the generic point of the henselian trait X_{0(s)} with finite residue field, and η̄ a geometric generic point of its strict henselisation X_{(s̄)} (cf. (1.7.1)). The fibre 𝓕_η̄ of 𝓕₀ at η̄ is a representation of the Weil group W(η̄/η); M denotes its local monodromy filtration (1.7.2).
items.note: DWP.5: 'Import LPV's inertia, nilpotent logarithm and monodromy-filtration carriers. Prove the local weight theorem for a punctually pure lisse sheaf on an open curve, including the weights of the monodromy graded pieces and the weights of boundary invariants of j_*F. Include quasi-unipotent reduction, finite covers, tensor and dual compatibility and the Frobenius–N relation' (Sources: 'especially 1.8.4').

items.name: Weight–monodromy for pure lisse sheaves on curves (Deligne's local theorem)
items.statement: With the notations of (1.8.1) and (1.8.3), if 𝓕₀ is punctually ι-pure of weight β, the representation Gr^M_i(𝓕_{0η̄}) of W(η̄/η) is ι-pure (1.7.4) of weight β+i.
items.note: Proof (p. 176): twist (1.2.7) to β = 0; pass to a finite cover so that ρ(σ) = exp(t_ℓ(σ)·N) on all of I. Then Ker N = 𝓕_{0η̄}^I is the fibre of j_*𝓕₀ at s̄, so by (1.8.1) eigenvalues of F on Ker N satisfy |ια| ≤ 1, hence by (1.6.14.2) also on P_{−i}. Applying this to 𝓕₀⊗𝓕₀ and (1.6.14.4): P_{−j}⊗P_{−j}(−j) is a direct factor of P₀ of the tensor square, so |ι(α²q^j)| ≤ 1, i.e. |ια| ≤ q^{−j/2}; applying it to the dual and (1.6.14.5) gives |ια| ≥ q^{−j/2}. So eigenvalues on P_{−j} have |ια| = q^{−j/2}, and one concludes by (1.6.14.3) (with the corrected twist,). DWP.5: 'Import LPV's inertia, nilpotent logarithm and monodromy-filtration carriers. Prove the local weight theorem for a punctually pure lisse sheaf on an open curve, including the weights of the monodromy graded pieces and the weights of boundary invariants of j_*F. Include quasi-unipotent reduction, finite covers, tensor and dual compatibility and the Frobenius–N relation' (Sources: 'especially 1.8.4'). The last step uses (1.6.14.3) with the corrected twist (PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E15).

items.name: For mixed lisse sheaves with pure graded pieces, the relative monodromy filtration exists and is the weight filtration
items.statement: Suppose 𝓕₀ lisse on U₀ with a finite increasing filtration W by lisse subsheaves such that each Gr^W_i(𝓕₀) is punctually ι-pure of weight i; let W also denote the induced filtration on 𝓕_η̄. Then 𝓕_η̄ is ι-mixed with integer weights, the local monodromy filtration of V [= 𝓕_η̄], rel. W (1.7.2) exists, and it coincides with the weight filtration of 𝓕_η̄ (1.7.5).
items.note: Proof: by (1.7.5) and (1.8.4) applied to the Gr^W_i(𝓕₀), the weight filtration satisfies the characteristic properties (1.6.13). DWP.5 plans the pure case (1.8.4) but no stage names the relative monodromy filtration. 'V' in the statement denotes 𝓕_η̄ (notation carried over from §1.7).

items.name: Set-up: tame sheaf along a smooth divisor over F_q with pure graded pieces
items.statement: Let D₀ be a smooth divisor in a scheme X₀ smooth over F_q, U₀ the complementary open, and 𝓕₀ a lisse sheaf on U₀ tamely ramified along D₀, with a finite increasing filtration W by lisse subsheaves such that Gr^W_i 𝓕₀ is punctually ι-pure of weight i (by (3.4) every lisse ι-mixed sheaf with integer punctual weights has such a filtration). Suppose D₀ defined by an equation t, and let 𝓕₀[D₀] be the sheaf on D₀ with an action of Z_ℓ(1) deduced by (1.7.8).
items.note: Forward reference to (3.4). Built on (1.7.8), which no stage plans.

items.name: Local monodromy filtration along a smooth divisor has pure graded pieces
items.statement: With the notations of (1.8.6), the local monodromy filtration around D of 𝓕₀[D₀], rel. W, exists. For this filtration, denoted M, Gr^M_i 𝓕₀[D₀] is punctually ι-pure of weight i.
items.note: Deduced from (1.8.5) by restricting 𝓕₀ to curves transverse to D₀. Generalised to normal crossings in §1.9.

items.name: Weights of the boundary stalks of j_*𝓕
items.statement: 1) With the notations of (1.8.1), if 𝓕₀ is lisse on U₀, (j_*𝓕)_s̄ = (𝓕_η̄)^I; it is obtained from Ker N by taking invariants under a finite group I/I₁. Under the hypotheses of (1.8.4), Ker N ⊂ M₀ (1.6). M thus induces on (j_*𝓕)_s̄ a filtration for which Gr^M_i(j_*𝓕)_s̄ is ι-pure of weight β+i and zero for i > 0. 2) Likewise, with the notations of (1.8.6), if 𝓕₀ is lisse on U₀ and tamely ramified along D₀, the restriction of j_*𝓕₀ to D₀ is the subsheaf of invariants of a finite group scheme μ_n in Ker N ⊂ 𝓕₀′[D₀]; if 𝓕₀ is punctually ι-pure of weight β one deduces by twisting from (1.8.7) that, for the monodromy filtration M, Gr^M_i(j_*𝓕₀|D₀) is punctually ι-pure of weight β+i, and zero for i > 0. 3) Under the hypotheses of (1.8.6), W and the monodromy define on j_*𝓕₀|D₀ a filtration M for which Gr^M_i(j_*𝓕₀|D₀) is lisse and ι-pure of weight i.
items.note: Part 1) is DWP.5's 'weights of boundary invariants of j_*F'; parts 2)–3) (divisor case) are not named in any stage. 2) is the input for the dévissage e) in (1.8.9). In 2) '𝓕₀′[D₀]' is presumably 𝓕₀[D₀].

items.name: j_* preserves ι-mixedness with punctual weights ≤ β
items.statement: Let X₀ be a scheme of finite type over F_q, j : U₀ ↪ X₀ an open subset, and 𝓕₀ an ι-mixed sheaf of punctual weights ≤ β on U₀. Then j_*𝓕₀ is again ι-mixed of punctual weights ≤ β. If the punctual weights of 𝓕₀ are integers, so are those of j_*𝓕₀.
items.note: Proof by induction on dim U₀ with dévissages justified by (1.2.5): a) extensions (left exactness of j_*); b) support: for i : V₀ ↪ U₀ locally closed with closure V̄₀ and 𝓕₀ ↪ i_*i*𝓕₀, replace (X₀,U₀,𝓕₀) by (V̄₀,V₀,i*𝓕₀); c) normalisation: for ε : X₀′ → X₀ finite surjective, j_*𝓕₀ ↪ ε_*j_*ε*𝓕₀; d) for 𝓕₀ lisse and k : V₀ ↪ U₀ dense open, j_*𝓕₀ ↪ (jk)_*k*𝓕₀; e) for X₀ normal, 𝓕₀ lisse, i : F₀ ↪ X₀ the complement of U₀ and k : V₀ ↪ F₀ dense open, i*j_*𝓕₀ ↪ k_*k*j_*𝓕₀ (normality makes the inverse image of U₀ in the strict henselisation connected). This reduces to X₀ normal, U₀ smooth, complement a Weil divisor F₀, 𝓕₀ lisse punctually ι-pure tamely ramified at the generic points of F₀, and then to (1.8.8) 2). DWP.8 plans 'f* and Rf_! preserve upper weights; f^! and Rf_* preserve lower weights' at complex level (derived from DWP.7), but not this sheaf-level upper bound for j_* (which is special to lisse/constructible ι-mixed sheaves). DWP.5 cites 'Weil II §§1.2–1.11' only as a source.

items.name: A lisse sheaf pure on a dense open is pure
items.statement: Let 𝓕₀ be a lisse sheaf on X₀ of finite type over F_q, and j : U₀ ↪ X₀ a dense open. If the restriction of 𝓕₀ to U₀ is punctually ι-pure, then 𝓕₀ itself is punctually ι-pure.
items.note: Proof: with β the weight of 𝓕₀|U₀, 𝓕₀ ↪ j_*j*𝓕₀ and 𝓕₀^∨ ↪ j_*j*𝓕₀^∨ (lisse); by (1.8.9) weights ≤ β and, for the dual, ≤ −β. Alternatively reduce to a smooth curve by restriction and normalisation and apply (1.8.1). No stage names it.

items.name: Lisse ι-mixed sheaves on normal schemes are successive extensions of punctually ι-pure lisse sheaves
items.statement: Every lisse ι-mixed sheaf 𝓕₀ on X₀ normal of finite type over F_q is a successive extension of lisse sheaves that are punctually ι-pure.
items.note: Proof: X₀ connected, reduce to 𝓕₀ irreducible; normality ⇒ its restriction to any nonempty open U₀ is irreducible, hence punctually ι-pure for suitable U₀ (definition of ι-mixed), then (1.8.10). Extended without normality in (3.4.1). DWP.8 plans the stronger 3.4.1 ('the unique functorial strict weight filtration on lisse mixed sheaves with integral weights') only for integral weights.

items.name: A lisse ι-mixed sheaf pure at one point of a connected base is pure
items.statement: Let 𝓕₀ be a lisse ι-mixed sheaf on X₀ connected of finite type over F_q. If 𝓕₀ is ι-pure at one point of X₀, it is punctually ι-pure.
items.note: Proof: for X₀ normal, (1.8.11) shows the weights of 𝓕₀ are read on its fibre at any point. In general apply (1.8.11) on the normalisation: the set of points where 𝓕₀ is pure of a given weight β contains, with a closed point x₀, all irreducible components through x₀; it is open and closed. No stage names it.

items.name: Variant: pure/mixed and integer-weight versions
items.statement: Throughout this paragraph (1.8) one may replace ι-pure and ι-mixed by 'pure' and 'mixed', as well as by 'ι-pure of integer weights' and 'ι-mixed of integer weights'.
items.note: DWP.5: 'Construct punctually ι-pure/ι-mixed lisse and constructible sheaves' and DWP.6 'Export both the fixed-ι real-weight theorem and the algebraic all-embeddings integer-weight theorem'.

items.name: Variation of mixed Hodge structures
items.statement: A 'variation of mixed Hodge structures' on a smooth analytic space S is the data of: a) a local system V_ℤ of free ℤ-modules of finite type; b) a finite increasing filtration W of V_ℚ = V_ℤ⊗ℚ by local subsystems of ℚ-vector spaces; c) a finite decreasing filtration F of 𝒱 = V_ℤ⊗𝒪 by vector subbundles (F varies holomorphically), satisfying Griffiths transversality ∇F^i ⊂ Ω¹⊗F^{i−1}, such that W and F define a mixed Hodge structure at each point of S.
items.note: Heuristic context only: in the dictionary of [2] I, (1.8.4) corresponds to W. Schmid's asymptotics of polarisable VHS on D*; (1.8.5) suggests Problem (1.8.15). Tau Ceti has mixed Hodge structures (library audit mentions their weight filtrations) but no variations.

items.name: Tame sheaf near a normal crossings divisor and its nearby sheaf 𝓕[E]
items.statement: Let X be a smooth scheme over 𝐅_q, D a divisor with normal crossings in X, the transverse union of smooth divisors D_i (i∈I), and E the intersection of the D_i. Assume each D_i is defined by a global equation t_i = 0, so that construction (1.7.8) applies (cf. however (1.7.10)). Let 𝓕 be a lisse sheaf on X − D, tamely ramified along D, admitting a finite increasing filtration W by lisse subsheaves such that Gr_i^W 𝓕 is punctually ι-pure of weight i. Let 𝐋 be the set of all primes ≠ p and define 𝓕[E] as in (1.7.8). It is a lisse sheaf on E with an action of 𝐙_𝐋(1)^I; this action is quasi-unipotent, whence 'endomorphisms' N_i : 𝓕[E](1) → 𝓕[E] (1.7.8).
items.note: (1.9) is explicitly 'not used in the sequel' (p. 179): it generalizes (1.8.7) to normal crossings divisors. The construction 𝓕[E] and N_i come from (1.7.8) (another section). The existence of W for any lisse ι-mixed sheaf with integral pointwise weights is forward-referenced to (3.4.1) (planned at DWP.8: 'the unique functorial strict weight filtration on lisse mixed sheaves with integral weights'). LPV.1 plans a single tame N and its monodromy filtration, not the several-variable nearby sheaf along an intersection of branches; no atlas stage plans this construction.

items.name: Relative monodromy condition L(W′, W″, (N_α)_{α∈A})
items.statement: Given a sheaf 𝒢, two finite increasing filtrations W′ and W″ of 𝒢, and a finite family of 'endomorphisms' N_α : 𝒢(1) → 𝒢 (α∈A), the condition L(W′, W″, (N_α)_{α∈A}) means: the N_α stabilize W′, satisfy N_α W″_a(1) ⊂ W″_{a−2}, and for all rational numbers c_α > 0 the endomorphism N = Σ c_α N_α induces isomorphisms N^b : (Gr^{W″}_{a+b} Gr^{W′}_a 𝒢)(b) ⥲ Gr^{W″}_{a−b} Gr^{W′}_a 𝒢.
items.note: A several-operator relative monodromy filtration condition. LPV.1 plans only the absolute monodromy filtration of one nilpotent ('Construct the uniquely characterized monodromy filtration centered at a specified integer'); the relative (1.6.13) version with several N_α and all positive rational combinations is not planned. The printed graded pieces read 'Gr^{W″}_{a+b} G^{W′}_a' (PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E23).

items.name: Uniqueness of W″ in condition L; integer coefficients suffice
items.statement: By (1.6.13), given W′ and the family (N_α), there exists at most one filtration W″ satisfying L(W′, W″, (N_α)_{α∈A}). In the statement of the condition one may replace 'rational number > 0' by 'integer > 0' (replace the c_α by n c_α and N by nN).
items.note: Uniqueness is the relative monodromy filtration uniqueness (1.6.13) of an earlier section. Used for the uniqueness half of (1.9.2) and to glue the pointwise filtrations in the proof of (1.9.3).

items.name: Existence and uniqueness of the system of weight filtrations W(J) on 𝓕[E]
items.statement: With the hypotheses and notation of (1.9.1), there exists on 𝓕[E] one and only one system of finite increasing filtrations W(J) (J ⊂ I) by lisse subsheaves stable under 𝐙_𝐋(1)^I (hence under the N_i) such that: a) W(∅) is the filtration deduced from W by functoriality; b) for J ⊂ K, the condition L(W(J), W(K), (N_k)_{k∈K−J}) holds. Moreover Gr_a^{W(I)} 𝓕[E] is punctually ι-pure of weight a.
items.note: Several-variable local monodromy-weight theorem for mixed tame sheaves along a normal crossings divisor. Uniqueness follows at once from (1.6.13), using only a) and b) for ∅ ⊂ K. Existence: (1.9.3) then (1.9.4). Not used later in the paper (p. 179). DWP.5 plans the curve case only ('Prove the local weight theorem for a punctually pure lisse sheaf on an open curve'); no stage plans the normal-crossings, several-N version.

items.name: Weight filtration for N = Σ c_k N_k along E
items.statement: Let (c_k)_{k∈I} be a system of integers > 0. The sheaf 𝓕[E] admits a (unique) finite increasing filtration W(I) by lisse subsheaves such that N = Σ c_k N_k satisfies the condition L(W, W(I), N). Moreover Gr_a^{W(I)} 𝓕[E] is punctually ι-pure of weight a.
items.note: Proof (pp. 180–181): by uniqueness (1.6.13) it suffices to find, at one geometric point x̄ of each connected component of E (localized at a closed point x, made rational by a finite extension of 𝐅_q), a filtration M on 𝓕[E]_x̄ satisfying L(W, M, N) with Gr_a^M pure of weight a; the pointwise filtrations then glue to a filtration by lisse subsheaves. Reduction to the curve case (1.8.5) (previous section, planned at DWP.5 'the weights of the monodromy graded pieces') via the key fact below. Also: W(I) is independent of the c_k, being characterized as the weight filtration ((1.9.4), p. 181).

items.name: Restriction to the monomial curve t_i = t^{c_i} identifies the monodromy logarithm with N
items.statement: With x a rational point of E, complete the t_i into local coordinates (t_i, u_j) centred at x (an étale map from a neighbourhood of x to affine space 𝐀^n sending x to the origin). Map the affine line (coordinate t) to 𝐀^n by t ↦ (t^{c_i}, 0), and let C be the fibre product of a neighbourhood of x with the affine line over 𝐀^n, with x (resp. x̄) the point (resp. geometric point) over x and over 0. On the strict localization C_(x̄), the geometric generic fibre of 𝓕 identifies with 𝓕[E]_x̄, and via this identification the logarithm of the local monodromy becomes N = Σ c_k N_k; hence (1.9.3) follows from (1.8.5).
items.note: Key step of the proof of (1.9.3); uses construction (1.7.8) and the curve local weight theorem (1.8.5) of an earlier section. Not planned: LPV.1/DWP.5 treat a single trait, not pullback along a monomial curve through a normal-crossings point.

items.name: Deduction of Theorem (1.9.2) from Lemma (1.9.3)
items.statement: The filtration W(I) of (1.9.3) does not depend on the choice of the c_k, being characterized independently of them as the filtration by weight. For J ⊂ I, with X_J, D_J and D*_J as in (1.7.9), applying (1.9.3) to X_J, the traces of the D_j (j∈J) and their intersection D*_J gives on 𝓕[D*_J] a weight filtration W(J) satisfying L(W, W(J), (N_j)_{j∈J}). Re-applying this to D_J, the traces of the D_i (i∉J) and 𝓕[D*_J] with the filtration W(J), one obtains for J ⊂ K on 𝓕[D*_J][D*_K] a weight filtration W(K) satisfying L(W(J), W(K), (N_i)_{i∈K−J}); via the isomorphism (1.7.9.1) 𝓕[D*_J][D*_K] ≅ 𝓕[D*_K] it coincides with the one constructed directly by (1.9.3), which satisfies L(W, W(K), (N_i)_{i∈K}) (uniqueness of the weight filtration). Since E = D_I, one defines W(J) on 𝓕[E] by functoriality from W(J) on 𝓕[D*_J] via 𝓕[E] = 𝓕[D*_J][E]; a) holds by definition and b) follows from L(W(J), W(K), (N_k)_{k∈K−J}) on 𝓕[D*_K].
items.note: Uses the iterated nearby-sheaf isomorphism (1.7.9.1) from an earlier section. Not planned by any atlas stage.

items.name: Relative variant of (1.9.2) over a base of finite type over 𝐙
items.statement: Let S be a scheme of finite type over 𝐙, f : X → S a smooth morphism, D ⊂ X a relative normal crossings divisor, and 𝓕 a lisse sheaf on X − D, tamely ramified along D. A variant of (1.9.2) holds in this setting; it is checked fibre by fibre, by reduction to (1.9.2). (By contrast, the case of a normal crossings divisor in a regular scheme S of finite type over 𝐙 seems inaccessible, already for S = Spec(𝐙[1/ℓ]).)
items.note: The variant is not stated precisely in the paper; recorded as stated. Not used later.

items.name: Hodge-theoretic analogue (Cattani–Kaplan), cited
items.statement: (Added in proof.) As explained in [2] I, one expects the theory of (polarizable) variations of Hodge structure to be often parallel to that of punctually pure lisse sheaves. With D* the punctured disc, Cattani and Kaplan have just proved an analogue of (1.9.2) (restricted to the pure case) for variations of Hodge structure on (D*)^I. In their context the c_α of condition L(W′, W″, (N_α)_{α∈A}) may even be taken real > 0 rather than rational > 0.
items.note: Cited external result (complex-analytic, Hodge theory); motivational only, not used. No atlas stage plans several-variable nilpotent orbit / variations of Hodge structure results of this kind.

items.name: Archimedean and non-archimedean coefficient absolute values
items.statement: Conventions (0.7) are in force. Let X_0 be a smooth absolutely irreducible curve over 𝐅_q, j : U_0 ↪ X_0 an open subset, complement of the finite set of points S_0, and 𝓕_0 a lisse sheaf on U_0. Choose either a) an isomorphism ι of 𝐐̄_ℓ with 𝐂 (archimedean case), or b) a prime ℓ′, an algebraic closure 𝐐̄_ℓ′ of 𝐐_ℓ′ and an isomorphism ι of 𝐐̄_ℓ with 𝐐̄_ℓ′ (non-archimedean case). The natural absolute value of 𝐐̄_ℓ′ is normalized, for example, by ‖ℓ′‖ = 1/ℓ′.
items.note: Extends the archimedean study of (1.8) (via the trace formula (1.4.7.2) and local monodromy) to non-archimedean absolute values of Frobenius eigenvalues. Only the archimedean ι-weight formalism is planned (DWP.0 'Define the separate ι-weight predicate'); the non-archimedean (ℓ′-adic / p-adic) valuation of eigenvalues via ι is not planned.
